extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent owners, and registered patent practitioners (agents/attorneys) filing appeals or briefs to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences (USPTO)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for taking an appeal from an examiner to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences (including notice of appeal, appeal brief content/timing, fees, remedies, and related procedural matters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may appeal / appeal eligibility (35 U.S.C. 134 and 37 CFR 1.191)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant (whose claims have been twice rejected), a patent owner in reexamination, or a third-party requester in an inter partes proceeding (subject to limits) may appeal to the Board; appeal must be taken by filing a notice of appeal and paying the fee within prescribed times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party requester may not appeal Board decisions; appeals available when claims have been 'twice or finally (§ 1.113) rejected' and the notice and fee are filed within the time periods of §§ 1.134 and 1.136. Jurisdiction passes to the Board upon transmittal of the file, including briefs and examiner's answers. Commissioner may sua sponte remand prior to decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Appeal requirements and recommended practice
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of appeal and fee must be filed within the allowed time; although rules no longer require identification of appealed claims or a signature, applicants should continue to identify claims and sign notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elimination of signature/claim-identification was to avoid redundant defects, but unsigned notices with unsigned authorizations (e.g., to charge a deposit account) may render the notice unacceptable. Use Form PTO/SB/31 (recommended). Office does not separately acknowledge receipt unless a self-addressed postcard is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for filing notice of appeal and effect of late filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of appeal must be filed within the period set in the last Office action (normally 3 months for reply) but may be filed up to 6 months from final rejection if accompanied by a petition and fee for extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely file a notice of appeal will result in abandonment of the application unless an extension under 37 CFR 1.136(a) (or applicable revival petition) is obtained. The date the notice, fee, and petition are filed governs the period of extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee requirements for appeal and brief (35 U.S.C. 41 / MPEP guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees are required for filing an appeal to the Board, filing the appeal brief, and requesting oral hearing; these are statutory/regulatory fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example statutory amounts cited: $300 for filing an appeal to the Board, $300 on filing a brief, and $260 for requesting an oral hearing (check current fee schedule/37 CFR 1.17 for current amounts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant's brief filing deadline and copies (37 CFR 1.192(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant must file a brief in triplicate within two months from the date of the notice of appeal or within the time allowed for reply to the action from which the appeal was taken (if later); the brief must be accompanied by the fee set forth in § 1.17(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file the brief with requisite fee within the time allowed will result in dismissal of the appeal. Time periods may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a) (or 1.136(b) for extraordinary circumstances) subject to limits discussed in MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the brief — overall requirement to set forth authorities and arguments (37 CFR 1.192(b),(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief must 'set forth the authorities and arguments on which appellant will rely' to maintain the appeal; any authorities or arguments not included will be refused consideration unless good cause is shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The brief must be responsive to every ground of rejection stated by the examiner; merely filing a paper titled 'brief' without the requisite substance will not comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief required item (1): Real party in interest (37 CFR 1.192(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement identifying the real party in interest, if the party named in the caption is not the real party in interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification helps Board members comply with ethics/conflict-of-interest rules. If not named, the examiner will assume the captioned party is the real party in interest; Board may nonetheless require explicit identification (see MPEP § 1210.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief required item (2): Related appeals and interferences (37 CFR 1.192(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement identifying by number and filing date all other appeals or interferences known to appellant that will directly affect or be directly affected by or have a bearing on the Board's decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List appeal/interference numbers and filing dates; statement not limited to copending applications. If none are identified, examiner will presume there are none, but the Board may require explicit identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief required item (3): Status of claims (37 CFR 1.192(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of the status of all claims in the application (pending, cancelled, allowed, rejected, etc.) and identification of each claim on appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to avoid confusion about which claims are on appeal and their precise wording; appellant's understanding of claim status assists examiner and Board in resolving disagreements before decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief required item (4): Status of amendments (37 CFR 1.192(c)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of the status of any amendment filed subsequent to final rejection (whether entered, denied entry, entered in part, or not acted upon).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This tells the examiner what the appellant considers the status of post-final amendments to be and allows resolution of disagreements before appeal is decided. Amendments should be filed as separate papers (not included in the appeal brief).

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief required item (5): Summary of the invention (37 CFR 1.192(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise explanation of the invention defined in the appealed claims, referring to the specification by page and line number and to drawings by reference characters, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferable to read the appealed claims on the specification and drawings; specificity (page/line) helps the Board quickly locate where claimed subject matter is described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief required item (6): Issues presented for review (37 CFR 1.192(c)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise statement of the issues presented for review; each stated issue should correspond to a separate ground of rejection appellant wishes the Board to review and must state the basis of the issue (not merely a conclusory statement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example of noncompliance: 'Whether claims 1 and 2 are unpatentable' is insufficient. Instead state the statutory basis and references, e.g., 'Whether claims 1 and 2 are unpatentable under 35 U.S.C. 103 over Smith in view of Jones.' The statement should not include argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief required item (7): Grouping of claims (37 CFR 1.192(c)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each ground of rejection contested that applies to a group of two or more claims, appellant must indicate whether the claims 'stand or fall together' or explicitly state they do not and provide arguments explaining separate patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant omits the statement and argument, it is a concession that the ground applies equally to all claims; the Board will select a single claim (generally the broadest) to decide the rejection unless appellant states otherwise and provides reasons. Mere pointing out differences is not sufficient—reasons for separate patentability must be argued in the Argument section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief required item (8): Argument — general rule and required subparts (37 CFR 1.192(c)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant's contentions on each issue presented and the basis therefor, with citations of authorities, statutes, and parts of the record relied on; each issue treated under a separate heading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes five subparagraphs (i)-(v) that prescribe what to include for common types of rejections (112 first and second paragraphs, 102, 103) and a general provision for other rejections. Arguments or authorities not included in the brief will be refused consideration unless good cause is shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument requirements for 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph (37 CFR 1.192(c)(8)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: For rejections under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, the argument must specify the errors in the rejection and how the first paragraph of 112 is complied with, including (as appropriate) how the specification and drawings (A) describe the subject matter defined by each rejected claim, (B) enable one skilled in the art to make and use the subject matter, and (C) set forth the best mode contemplated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific as to how the specification/drawings satisfy description/enablement/best mode for each rejected claim; a general statement is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument requirements for 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph (37 CFR 1.192(c)(8)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: For rejections under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, the argument must specify the errors in the rejection and how the claims particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter applicant regards as the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why claim language satisfies the definiteness requirement; point to claim language and record to rebut examiner's position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument requirements for 35 U.S.C. 102 rejections (37 CFR 1.192(c)(8)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: For rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102, the argument must specify the errors and why the rejected claims are patentable under 102, including specific claim limitations not described in the prior art relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the particular claim limitations absent from the asserted reference(s) and explain why those differences render the claims novel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument requirements for 35 U.S.C. 103 rejections (37 CFR 1.192(c)(8)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: For rejections under 35 U.S.C. 103, the argument must specify the errors and, where appropriate, identify specific claim limitations not described in the prior art and explain how such limitations render the claimed subject matter unobvious; if rejection is based on a combination of references, explain why the references, taken as a whole, do not suggest the claimed subject matter and why features from different references should not be combined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A general argument that limitations are not all disclosed in a single reference is insufficient; explain non-obviousness and the inappropriateness of combining references when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument for other rejections (37 CFR 1.192(c)(8)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: For any rejection other than those specifically covered by (i)-(iv), the argument must specify the errors in the rejection and the specific limitations in the rejected claims (if appropriate) or other reasons which cause the rejection to be in error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor the argument to the statutory/ground basis of the rejection (e.g., 101 subject-matter issues may not require pinpointing claim limitations but should explain why the rejection is erroneous).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix requirement (37 CFR 1.192(c)(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: An appendix containing a copy of the claims involved in the appeal must be included with the brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant relies on any references, appellant is expected to provide the Board with three copies of such references. The brief must be filed in triplicate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of not filing a compliant brief (37 CFR 1.192(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a brief does not comply with paragraph (c), the appellant will be notified of reasons for non-compliance and given one month to file an amended brief; failure to file an adequate amended brief will result in dismissal of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no brief is filed and an amendment filed within the filing period places the application in condition for allowance, the amendment may be entered; otherwise dismissal stands. Oral argument will not cure a deficient brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant must address every ground of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant's brief must be responsive to every ground of rejection stated by the examiner; failure to address any ground will result in notification and requirement to correct the deficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if appellant believes a ground is 'clearly improper', the brief must explain why. Not addressing a ground can lead to non-compliance notices (forms cited) and cannot be cured by oral argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro se appellant brief standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief filed by an appellant pro se (not prepared/signed by a registered practitioner) will be accepted if it substantially complies with items (1), (2), and (8) of 37 CFR 1.192(c); if accepted, it will be presumed that all claims of a rejected group stand or fall together unless the pro se brief presents reasons why claims are separately patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pro se appellants have relaxed content requirements but should still address the key items; absence of arguments vs. unconvincing arguments are treated differently (lack of any argument triggers notification of defect).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time measurement for the two-month brief period (office receipt date rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office date of receipt of the Notice of Appeal (not Certificate of Mailing date) is the date from which the two-month period for filing the brief is measured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 512 for mailing/receipt nuances. 37 CFR 1.192(a) alternatively allows filing within the time allowed for reply to the action from which the appeal was taken if that is later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time to file the brief (37 CFR 1.136)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant may petition for an extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) (with fee) to file the brief; additional time in excess of 5 months will not be granted unless extraordinary circumstances under 1.136(b) are shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time extended is added to the calendar day of the original period. If 1.136(a) is not available, 1.136(b) may provide relief for extraordinary circumstances. Proper petitions and fees must be filed timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal dismissal and effect on allowed claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If the appeal is dismissed for failure to file the brief (and some claims are allowed), the application does not become abandoned as to allowed claims and is returned to the examiner for action on the allowed claims; if no claims are allowed, the application is abandoned as of the date the brief was due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims objected to as dependent from a rejected claim do not stand allowed. In reexamination proceedings, failure to file the brief will result in issuance of the certificate under 37 CFR 1.570.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices of Appeal unacceptable — common defects (form ¶¶ 12.01–12.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: Common reasons a Notice of Appeal is unacceptable include unpaid appeal fee, absence of a second or final rejection, untimely filing, or the claims already being allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fee unpaid, applicant may obtain extension under 37 CFR 1.136(a). For untimely filings, the date of filing the notice, fee, and petition determine extension period. If a notice is unacceptable because claims are allowed, it will be rejected as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special-case prosecution through appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: An application made special and advanced out of turn will remain special throughout prosecution in the PTO, including any appeal to the Board, provided the applicant prosecutes diligently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition to make an application special after the appeal has been forwarded to the Board may be addressed to the Board but will not be granted unless the brief has been filed and applicant makes the same type of showing required under 37 CFR 1.102; diligent prosecution is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments filed with or after appeal — form and entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments should not be included in the appeal brief but filed as separate papers; if an amendment filed within the period for filing the brief places the application in condition for allowance, it may be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 1207, 1215.01, and 1215.02. The Office retains pending status during the brief filing period so that prosecution may continue by filing amendments separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of references relied upon in brief
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant relies on some reference in the brief, appellant is expected to provide the Board with three copies of the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide copies of relied references may impede consideration; include copies in triplicate as required for the brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board selection of single claim from a group when claims stand or fall together
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appellant does not state that claims in a rejected group do not stand or fall together and does not argue separate patentability, the Board will normally select a single claim (often the broadest) from the group and decide the rejection on that claim alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If separate patentability is asserted, appellant must state so and present reasons in the Argument section. Examples and case law cited (In re Young; In re Nielson; In re King; In re Sernaker) illustrate the practice and rationale to promote efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional and procedural notes (remand and transmittal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Jurisdiction over the application passes to the Board upon transmittal of the file (including briefs and examiner's answers); prior to Board decision the Commissioner may remand to the examiner; the Chief Administrative Patent Judge may substitute a Board member if one who heard the appeal cannot participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may also remand to consider amendments, affidavits, or declarations. If a hearing member becomes unavailable after hearing but before decision, the Chief may substitute another member without rehearing or offer a rehearing to the appellant (see In re Bose Corp.).
